general_reasoning: Policy section1(6) prefers publication on an ambiguous but defensible basis, with explicit reasoning. This recommendation is a qualified project judgment, not a declaration that the1962 edition or every element of its revisions is public domain.

The source foundation is a complete independently identified1922 prayer for each case, plus the separately identified traditional conclusion control where needed. It is not a reconstruction of a modern whole prayer from scattered older phrases. Those historical expressions retain their own public-domain basis; any later contribution must be assessed separately.

The Copyright Office’s Circular14 distinguishes preexisting material from new original authorship in derivative works. Circular33 and37CFR202.1(a) support the limited authorship in individual words and short expressions. These provisions do not decide every combination of short changes automatically. All measured modern contributions are assessed in their prayer context together, not merely counted or excused one by one.

The originality threshold is low and a semantic revision can be original. The affirmative case here is the limited expressive contribution of the exact whole measured revision, with no newly authored petition/clause or new literary architecture beyond the identified conventional substitutions, factual title, case form, options and old conclusion. This supports qualified-nonoriginal-adaptation for these three specific hashes; uncertainty remains explicit.

Prior latin-seven and Joseph-clause decisions supply examples of separately bounded procedure only. None grants permission for these cases, and none substitutes for the substantive counsel-to-wisdom assessment.

cases.complete_contribution_assessment: The consilii→sapientiae substitution changes counsel to wisdom and is substantive. It is not functional, orthographic or a historical identity. In this exact source-fixed prayer the new expression is nevertheless one ordinary abstract noun occupying the same existing spiritum ... et fortitudinis construction. Atque Doctori adds a factual rank in the existing Confessori tuo address; gloria→gloriam is a case-ending variation, preserved despite its incongruity, not a new expressive clause. The longer ending is an independently controlled contiguous traditional formula prefix, not newly composed wording. Considering all those changes together, without atomising away their combined effect, the modern contribution remains a slight conventional revision within the same old complete petition, and a qualified insufficient-originality basis is defensible.
cases.strong_counterargument_and_response: This is the strongest contrary case: replacing counsel with wisdom in association with a newly stated Doctor rank can be a deliberate theological/editorial revision, and copyright requires little creativity. A semantic change is not immunised by being one word, and a combination of otherwise ordinary words can be original. A court could assess the revision more broadly. The recommendation rests on the measured combined expression and preserved syntax/petition, factual title and separately old conclusion, not on a universal word-count exemption or an assertion that meaning is unchanged.
